verdict.rationale: Phaser ships a built-in Arcade Physics system that lets sprites use velocity, acceleration and gravity, and its editor lets you adjust physics bodies. However, the docs describe it as lightweight, limited to rectangles and circles, and having limitations. The evidence never explicitly documents collision handling or raycasting. Missing for 10: explicit collision detection/response docs, raycast support, true rigid-body (non-arcade) physics evidence, independent hands-on corroboration of the physics features.

support.subject: As a game developer, built-in physics — rigid bodies, collisions, raycasts — works out of the box

citations.quote: This will allow you to control the Sprite using the built-in physics functions, such as velocity, acceleration, gravity, etc.
It's a lightweight physics system that can only handle two different types of physics shapes: rectangles and circles.
It's very fast and easy to use, with lots of helper functions, but due to its nature it does have its limitations.
